request.system_prompt:
You are the defect reviewer agent of LANSH, a factory that migrates legacy SAS 9.4 jobs to PySpark. LANSH reproduces every legacy behaviour exactly, bugs included, and asks a person to decide what to do about each suspected bug, so finding them matters.

Read the job and list the places where the code most likely does not do what its author intended: wrong comparisons or boundaries, joins that multiply rows, gaps or overlaps in bands, wrong date columns, missing values handled wrongly, truncation, hard-coded constants that should vary. Ignore style, performance and things that are merely unusual. For each, write one Spark SQL SELECT over the views listed that measures the impact on the legacy output: it must return exactly one row with rows_affected (the output rows the bug changes) and, when the bug changes an amount, amount_affected (the total change, positive). Compare what the legacy output holds with what the intended logic would give. Use only the views and columns listed.

defects.description: Both PROC MEANS steps use CLASS lob_code prem_band without the MISSING option, so SAS discards every observation whose class variable is missing. lob_code comes from each policy's first-loaded transaction (work.policy_band), so when that row has a blank lob_code, all of that policy's transactions and the policy itself are left out of rpt.premium_band_summary. Written and earned premium are understated.
defects.impact_query: WITH o AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, written_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY _row_seq) AS rn FROM dw_fact_premium_earned), pb AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, CASE WHEN written_eur IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN written_eur < 0 THEN 'NEGATIVE' WHEN written_eur < 250 THEN '0-249' WHEN written_eur < 500 THEN '250-499' WHEN written_eur < 1000 THEN '500-999' ELSE '1000+' END AS prem_band FROM o WHERE rn = 1) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pb.prem_band) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(ABS(SUM(t.written_eur)), 0) AS amount_affected FROM dw_fact_premium_earned t JOIN pb ON t.policy_id = pb.policy_id WHERE pb.lob_code IS NULL OR TRIM(pb.lob_code) = ''
defects.intended_behaviour: Every transaction should be reported. Policies with a missing line of business should appear in their own (blank or UNKNOWN) lob_code group, for example via the CLASS ... / MISSING option, rather than being dropped.
defects.title: Policies with missing lob_code silently dropped by PROC MEANS CLASS

defects.description: The as_of parameter is only stamped onto the output (line 74). Nothing filters dw.fact_premium_earned to transactions on or before the reporting date, so transactions dated after 2025-12-31 are counted in n_transactions, written_eur and earned_eur.
defects.impact_query: WITH o AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, written_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY _row_seq) AS rn FROM dw_fact_premium_earned), pb AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, CASE WHEN written_eur IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN written_eur < 0 THEN 'NEGATIVE' WHEN written_eur < 250 THEN '0-249' WHEN written_eur < 500 THEN '250-499' WHEN written_eur < 1000 THEN '500-999' ELSE '1000+' END AS prem_band FROM o WHERE rn = 1) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pb.lob_code, pb.prem_band) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(ABS(SUM(t.written_eur)), 0) AS amount_affected FROM dw_fact_premium_earned t JOIN pb ON t.policy_id = pb.policy_id WHERE t.txn_date > DATE'2025-12-31' AND pb.lob_code IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(pb.lob_code) <> ''
defects.intended_behaviour: Only transactions with txn_date on or before &as_of (2025-12-31) should be included in the report as at that date.
defects.title: No as-of cut-off: transactions after the reporting date included

defects.description: PROC SORT NODUPKEY BY policy_id keeps whichever transaction was loaded first for each policy, and that row's written_eur (and lob_code) sets the band for all the policy's transactions. If the load order differs from transaction order, a later endorsement, cancellation or negative adjustment can set the band, and the policy moves to a different band (or line of business), possibly NEGATIVE.
defects.impact_query: WITH r AS (SELECT policy_id, lob_code, written_eur, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY _row_seq) AS rn_load, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY policy_id ORDER BY txn_date ASC NULLS LAST, _row_seq) AS rn_date FROM dw_fact_premium_earned), b AS (SELECT policy_id, rn_load, rn_date, lob_code, CASE WHEN written_eur IS NULL THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN written_eur < 0 THEN 'NEGATIVE' WHEN written_eur < 250 THEN '0-249' WHEN written_eur < 500 THEN '250-499' WHEN written_eur < 1000 THEN '500-999' ELSE '1000+' END AS band FROM r WHERE rn_load = 1 OR rn_date = 1), p AS (SELECT policy_id, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_load = 1 THEN lob_code END) AS l_lob, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_load = 1 THEN band END) AS l_band, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_date = 1 THEN lob_code END) AS i_lob, MAX(CASE WHEN rn_date = 1 THEN band END) AS i_band FROM b GROUP BY policy_id), d AS (SELECT * FROM p WHERE NOT (l_lob <=> i_lob AND l_band <=> i_band)), g AS (SELECT l_lob AS lob, l_band AS band FROM d WHERE l_lob IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(l_lob) <> '' UNION SELECT i_lob, i_band FROM d WHERE i_lob IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(i_lob) <> '') SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM g) AS rows_affected, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(ABS(t.written_eur)) FROM dw_fact_premium_earned t JOIN d ON t.policy_id = d.policy_id), 0) AS amount_affected
defects.intended_behaviour: Band each policy on its true opening transaction: the earliest txn_date, with load order breaking ties.
defects.title: Policy band taken from first-loaded row, not the earliest (opening) transaction
